title: Finite loopless multigraph rigidity from its cycle lattice
statement: Let $V$ and $E$ be finite sets, and for every $e\in E$ specify an unordered pair of distinct vertices as its endpoints. This is a finite loopless multigraph $\Gamma$, with parallel edges allowed; the degree of a vertex counts incident edges with multiplicity. Choose an orientation of each edge and let $H_1(\Gamma,\mathbf Z)=\ker(\partial:\mathbf Z^E\to\mathbf Z^V)$, where $\partial e=t(e)-s(e)$ and $\mathbf Z^S$ is the free abelian group on $S$. This cycle group is a free abelian group of finite rank [lem-weil-subgroup-finite-free-abelian-group-free]. An automorphism $\sigma$ consists of permutations of $V,E$ preserving endpoint pairs. It induces a signed permutation on $\mathbf Z^E$, with a minus sign when the chosen orientation is reversed, and hence an action on $H_1(\Gamma,\mathbf Z)$. If $\sigma$ fixes every vertex of degree at most two and acts as the identity on $H_1(\Gamma,\mathbf Z)$, then it fixes every vertex and every edge. No connectedness assumption is required.

proof.text: Use strong induction on $N=|V|+|E|$, with the assertion quantified over all loopless multigraphs and all automorphisms satisfying the two hypotheses. The case $N=0$ is empty. Changing an edge orientation multiplies its coordinate by $-1$, conjugating the boundary and automorphism operators; thus it preserves the identity-on-kernel hypothesis. Below choose convenient orientations for the affected edges and retain all others. Every reduced graph has strictly smaller $N$.

source.place: Printed p.86, graph argument after Lemma 1.17: induction parameter

proof.text: If $x$ has degree zero, it is fixed. Remove $x$. All other degrees and the cycle kernel are unchanged, so the restriction satisfies the hypotheses. Induction fixes every remaining vertex and edge, and hence the original graph.

If $x$ has degree one, it is fixed; its unique incident edge $e=\{x,y\}$ is fixed and so is $y$. Remove $x,e$. For an integral cycle, its boundary coefficient at $x$ forces its $e$-coordinate to vanish, so extension by zero identifies the new cycle kernel equivariantly with the old one. Only $y$ changes degree, and $y$ is already fixed; hence every new vertex of degree at most two is fixed. Induction on the reduced graph and fixedness of $x,e$ give the conclusion.

Suppose $\deg(x)=2$, with distinct incident edges $e_1,e_2$ both joining $x$ to the same vertex $y$. The vertex $x$ is fixed, and $y$ is fixed as its only neighbour. Orient both edges from $x$ to $y$. Their difference $e_1-e_2$ is a nonzero integral cycle. Interchanging the two edges would negate this cycle, contradicting identity on the cycle kernel; thus both edges are fixed individually. Remove $x,e_1,e_2$. Extension by zero embeds the new cycle kernel equivariantly into the old one, so its action is identity. Only $y$ changes degree and it is fixed. Induction now fixes the reduced graph and thus the original graph.

source.place: Printed pp.86–87, first degree-two case (parallel edges)

proof.text: Suppose instead the two edges at the fixed degree-two vertex $x$ join it to distinct vertices $y,z$. Replace $y\! -\! x\! -\! z$ by one new edge $a=\{y,z\}$. This is loopless, and $\sigma$ descends because it preserves the two-edge path setwise. Orient the path as $y\to x\to z$ and $a$ as $y\to z$. In a cycle the two path coefficients agree, by its boundary coefficient at $x$. Replacing their common value by the $a$-coefficient gives an isomorphism of integral cycle kernels, with inverse replacing $a$ by the sum of the path edges. It commutes with the action: if $y,z$ are swapped, both the oriented path and $a$ acquire a minus sign; otherwise neither does. All retained vertex degrees are unchanged, so the reduced graph satisfies both hypotheses. Induction fixes its vertices and edges. Consequently $y,z$ are fixed individually; since $x$ is fixed, the two original edges are fixed individually as well. All other edges and vertices were unchanged, giving the conclusion.

We may now assume all degrees are at least three. If an edge $e=\{x,y\}$ and both its endpoints are fixed, delete $e$. Extension by zero embeds the new integral cycle kernel equivariantly into the old one, hence its action is identity. Only $x,y$ lose degree, and they are already fixed. Every low-degree vertex of the reduced graph is therefore fixed. Induction fixes this graph, and $e$ was fixed too. This proves the assertion in this case.

source.place: Printed p.87, fixed edge with fixed endpoints reduction

proof.text: It remains that $V\ne\varnothing$, all degrees are at least three, and there are no fixed edges with individually fixed endpoints. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-graph-euler-trace], writing $b=\dim_{\mathbf Q}Z_1$ and $c=|\pi_0|$. The action on $Z_1$ is identity: multiplying any rational cycle by a common positive denominator makes it integral, where the action is identity, and then divide back. Thus its trace is $b$. We have $f_+=0$, $f_0,f_-\ge0$, and $f_c\le c$. Counting incidences gives $2|E|=\sum_v\deg(v)\ge3|V|$, so $|E|>|V|$ and the dimension formula yields $b=|E|-|V|+c>c$. The trace identity would give $0\le f_0+f_-=f_c-b\le c-b<0$, a contradiction. If $V$ is empty, looplessness forces $E$ empty, already covered by the base case. All induction cases are exhausted.

lean.statement: theorem finiteGraphHomologyRigidity (V : Type u) (E : Type v) [Finite V] [Fintype E] [DecidableEq V] (s t : E → V) (_hne : ∀ e : E, s e ≠ t e) : (∃ r : ℕ, Nonempty (Module.Basis (Fin r) ℤ (LinearMap.ker (Finsupp.linearCombination ℤ (fun e : E ↦ Finsupp.single (t e) (1 : ℤ) - Finsupp.single (s e) 1))))) ∧ ∀ (σV : Equiv.Perm V) (σE : Equiv.Perm E), (∀ e : E, (σV (s e) = s (σE e) ∧ σV (t e) = t (σE e)) ∨ (σV (s e) = t (σE e) ∧ σV (t e) = s (σE e))) → (∀ x : V, (Finset.univ.filter (fun e : E ↦ s e = x ∨ t e = x)).card ≤ 2 → σV x = x) → (∀ c : E →₀ ℤ, Finsupp.linearCombination ℤ (fun e : E ↦ Finsupp.single (t e) (1 : ℤ) - Finsupp.single (s e) 1) c = 0 → Finsupp.linearCombination ℤ (fun e : E ↦ if σV (s e) = s (σE e) then Finsupp.single (σE e) (1 : ℤ) else -Finsupp.single (σE e) 1) c = c) → σV = Equiv.refl V ∧ σE = Equiv.refl E
